teams.name: Reticet
teams.description:
Reticet: speech to a case record where nothing is written that was not said.

A protection officer finishes an interview in a displacement setting and has minutes to write it up before the next one. That note is what triggers a referral, or fails to. Voice tools built for meetings transcribe and summarise it confidently, including the parts they got wrong. A confident wrong summary is worse than no summary, because it gets acted on and an empty field gets checked.

Reticet takes the write-up, not the interview. No survivor is ever recorded. A field worker speaks a case note in English or French, and every populated field has to point at the exact words they said. If those words are not in the transcript, the field stays blank with the reason showing. When the worker says "names I did not get" or "I'm not certain", the system may not fill that field at all.

Built on AssemblyAI streaming speech to text. The claim is calibrated abstention.

teams.description:
RevenueFlow — the reception desk that actually listens.

In Latin America, WhatsApp isn't a channel: it's the phone. Small businesses
run inside it, and their customers don't type — they talk. Every CRM shows a
voice note as a grey box saying "audio message", and a human still has to
listen, understand, open a calendar and reply.

RevenueFlow turns a Spanish or Portuguese WhatsApp voice note into a booked
appointment in ~7 seconds, and replies to the customer. Built on AssemblyAI:
Universal-3.5 Pro biased with the business's own service catalog, plus LLM
Gateway for intent against a strict schema.

The rule it rests on: the model decides what the customer wants, the system
decides what's allowed. It cannot invent a service, a date or availability.
It remembers the conversation, so "better Friday" reschedules the right
appointment.

Live, with real WhatsApp: revenueflow-ai-yanero.vercel.app

teams.name: Roxi AI
teams.description:
Roxi AI is a real-time multi-agent meeting co-pilot that records audio of meetings to provide live strategic and technical insights. Going beyond post-meeting transcription, Roxi analyzes audio instantly using a Rust/Tauri core with OS-level loopback. A Node.js sidecar handles seamless failover of STT providers via a ring-buffer to avoid data loss.
For reduced LLM latency and cost, a Rust ChunkGraph orchestrator analyzes utterance complexity within milliseconds. Chit-chat is ignored, and parallel AI agents—such as Risk Detectors and Technical Analysts—are launched instantly only on dense topics, showing live insights. All data is locally saved in SQLite database, analyzed post-meeting using an Adaptive-RAG chatbot.
Roxi AI is built after overcoming challenging macOS audio routing and IPC framing issues. Future plans include advanced speaker diarization, proactively taking action during meetings, and full offline local LLM capabilities.
